problems.title: Even or Odd
problems.statement:
Read one integer n.
Print EVEN if n is even, otherwise print ODD.

Input
One line with one integer n (1 <= n <= 10^9).

Output
Print EVEN or ODD on one line.

Example
Input: 7
Output: ODD

problems.title: Count Vowels
problems.statement:
Read one line of text. Count how many vowels it contains.
Vowels are a, e, i, o, u in either upper or lower case.

Input
One line of text (at most 1000 characters, letters and spaces).

Output
Print the number of vowels.

Example
Input: Hello World
Output: 3

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.statement:
You are given a sequence of n integers a1, a2, ..., an.
A subsequence is obtained by deleting zero or more elements without changing the order
of the rest. A subsequence is strictly increasing if each element is larger than the one before it.

Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

Input
The first line contains n (1 <= n <= 50000).
The second line contains n integers ai (-10^9 <= ai <= 10^9).

Output
Print one integer: the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

Example
Input:
6
10 9 2 5 3 7
Output:
3
(One such subsequence is 2 5 7 or 2 3 7.)

problems.title: Shortest Paths from City 1
problems.statement:
There are n cities numbered 1 to n and m two-way roads. Road i connects cities ui and vi
and has length wi. Roads may form cycles, and some cities may be unreachable.

For every city i from 1 to n, find the length of the shortest path from city 1 to city i.
The distance from city 1 to itself is 0. If city i cannot be reached, print -1.

Input
The first line contains n and m (2 <= n <= 20000, 1 <= m <= 40000).
Each of the next m lines contains ui, vi, wi (1 <= ui, vi <= n, ui != vi, 1 <= wi <= 10^6).

Output
Print n integers separated by single spaces: the distances for cities 1..n.

Example
Input:
4 4
1 2 1
2 3 2
1 3 5
3 4 1
Output:
0 1 3 4
